newsitem.title: USA: Duke says Fran power outages drop to 65,000.
newsitem.headline: Duke says Fran power outages drop to 65,000.

text.p: Duke Power Co, one of the southeastern U.S. utilities hardest hit by hurricane Fran, said Monday it still has about 65,000 customers without electricity.

This was a sharp drop from Friday when, according to the company's latest tally, 431,000 customers lost power as the storm swept across North Carolina, hitting northeastern parts Duke's service territory.
"The service area looks like a giant stomped all over it," said Steve Cranfill, one of Duke Power's storm directors, after surveying the storm damage by helicopter this weekend.
Duke, based in Charlotte, N.C., said the bulk of those still lacking electricity - about 45,000 - are in the Durham, N.C. area, where service is expected to be restored by mid-week.
"We have about 12,000 miles of transmission lines. A dozen transmission circuits were affected at the height of the storm. All of these have been restored," said company spokesman Joe Maher.
He said none of Duke's generating facilities was hurt by Fran and saw no problems meeting peak electricity demand today on its system, though he did not have a load forecast immediately available.
The company said about 1,800 of its own personnel and 1,000 emergency workers from other southern utilities were working to restore power.
Duke has about 1.8 million customers in western and central North Carolina and South Carolina.
